paper_title: TL;DR Too Long, Do Re-weighting for Effcient LLM Reasoning Compression
caption: Comparison of accuracy and generation length between Vanilla CoT and our method on four benchmark datasets (GSM8K, MATH500, AIME, AMC) using DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen models. consistently reduces generation length while maintaining or improving accuracy across both 7B and 14B model scales.
model_annotation: The grouped vertical bar chart, titled "DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B Generation Length Comparison," illustrates generation lengths for two distinct methods across four benchmark datasets. The horizontal axis represents the benchmark categories, ordered from left to right as GSM8K, MATH500, AIME, and AMC, without an explicit axis label. The vertical value axis is labeled "Generation Length (words)" and features a linear scale ranging from 0 to over 8000, with numeric tick labels provided at regular intervals of 1000, accompanied by light gray dashed horizontal gridlines. The data is organized into side-by-side paired bars for each category. According to the top-center legend, light pink bars represent "Vanilla CoT," positioned on the left of each pair, while dark red bars represent "TLDR (Ours)," positioned on the right. The exact generation lengths for the Vanilla CoT method are explicitly annotated in black text above each light pink bar: 554 for GSM8K (representing the shortest group), 2861 for MATH500, 6820 for AIME (representing the tallest group), and 4510 for AMC. The TLDR (Ours) dark red bars are consistently shorter than their corresponding Vanilla CoT bars in every category. Above each dark red bar, a red text annotation indicates a percentage: "-54%" for GSM8K, "-46%" for MATH500, "-7%" for AIME, and "-25%" for AMC. The categories are not sorted in a strictly alphabetical or numerical order, and visual emphasis is primarily applied through the explicitly labeled data points and red percentage text annotating the bars.
